items.text: The Justice Department filed a federal suit in Alaska on Oct 22 asking that the state be barred from certifying a win by Democrat Mary Peltola over Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) while a same-named candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan, stays on the ballot. On Oct 23 Trump said he told DOJ to file it, and by Oct 24 Democrats and voting-rights groups were challenging it, according to a CNBC headline. Attorney General Todd Blanche said DOJ does not intend to interfere improperly with state certification. A Notre Dame election-law scholar told AP the statute does not let DOJ block certification.
items.reporter: Associated Press; Katherine Faulders et al. (ABC)
items.outlet: AP via Alaska Public Media; ABC News
items.notes: The suit was filed Oct 22, just before the time window, so the news in the window is Trump's admission and the challenge. I could not open the CNBC story about the challenge (fetch failed). Breitbart (Oct 23) framed the suit as defending election integrity and quoted no opposing side. AP and ABC included Democratic criticism and expert doubts. Daniel J. Sullivan won about 2% of the August primary vote.

items.text: On Oct 25 a Ninth Circuit panel heard DOJ's emergency bid to make California set aside mail ballots from roughly 20,000 registered voters that federal agencies flagged as likely noncitizens. Live accounts say the panel, including Judges Bennett and Sanchez, doubted it had jurisdiction because the district court had not ruled yet. The judges also questioned whether the Elections Clause lets DOJ tell a state which votes to count. California argues DOJ lacks standing and that the request breaks the NVRA's 90-day rule and the Purcell principle. U.S. District Judge David O. Carter has a hearing set for Tuesday, Oct 27.
items.reporter: Rick Hasen (Election Law Blog); Zachary Fedyk (JURIST)
items.outlet: Election Law Blog; JURIST; CNN; Fox News
items.notes: Hasen's post was written during the argument and marked 'in progress'. I saw CNN's headline (judges skeptical) but could not open the page. Fox News (Sinkewicz/Finn) led with DOJ's claims and those of Bill Essayli, who said noncitizens had very likely already voted in LA County, and put California's objections lower down. Los Angeles County says ballots that have already been processed cannot be traced back to voters. Ninth Circuit case no. 26-7070.

items.text: With the Nov 3 midterms about a week away, Trump rallied on Oct 25 in Port Huron, Michigan, for Senate nominee Mike Rogers and gubernatorial nominee John James. Barack Obama campaigned in Detroit on Oct 24 for Democrats Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson. Trump attacked El-Sayed on Truth Social, and the Times of Israel reported he said Jews who vote for El-Sayed should be ashamed. The Fox live blog cites Reuters for the current balance: Republicans hold the House 218-214 and the Senate 53-47, so Democrats need a net gain of four seats in each chamber.
items.notes: Most items in the live blog are partisan claims. Speaker Johnson called recent national polls 'wrong' and said they undersample Republicans, and campaign-released internal polls are unverified. I found no independent final-week polling in the window. The most recent independent polls I saw were NYT/Siena in September (Democrats about +9 on the generic ballot among likely voters) and WaPo-Ipsos in July (Democrats +3). Both are stale. Trump's schedule this week: Mississippi on Mon, Texas on Tue, Ohio on Wed (Gray DC).

items.text: On Oct 25 Trump told reporters there would be no US strike on Iran that day. That contradicted US envoy Tom Barrack, who had said a weekend strike was possible. Trump also said more strikes before the Nov 3 midterms were possible but that a 'big, beautiful' agreement was too. Iran's President Pezeshkian accused Washington of disrupting talks. The talks are stalled despite a memorandum of understanding signed in June, and the US says it is still enforcing a naval blockade of Iran's ports.
items.outlet: TASS; Times of Israel; ABC News
items.notes: TASS is Russian state media. Times of Israel reported the same Trump remarks about possible strikes or a deal. I found no AP or Reuters text for these remarks (search budget ran out). ABC's live blog (Shalvey/Brennan/El-Bawab) gives background on the stalled MOU and ongoing exchanges of strikes at a lower intensity.

items.text: An unclassified Oct 23 memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US officials abroad, and a US official confirmed the memo to ABC News. Two senior Iranian officials told the New York Times that US diplomats and personnel are fair targets. The State Department is reportedly cutting staff at embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE and has ordered non-essential staff out of Saudi Arabia.
items.outlet: ABC News; New York Times (via Times of Israel)
items.notes: The memo is confirmed by ABC and reported by the NYT. The embassy drawdowns and the claim that Iran has operatives inside the US come from the NYT as relayed by Times of Israel; I did not see an official State Department notice. UKMTO reported on Oct 23 that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.text: On Oct 23 Trump signed a proclamation that again changes which Canadian goods face the 50% Section 338 duties. The duties were first imposed in July over Canada's motor-vehicle tariffs. Trade-compliance firm GHY says the changes take effect Oct 30. They remove some plywood, paper products, machinery, refrigeration equipment and packing crates, and add some valves, carpets and waste products. This continues a US-Canada tariff escalation that in September added outright import bans on some Canadian goods.
items.notes: I did not see the annex text, so the exact product changes come from GHY's summary. CBP guidance was still pending. On the campaign trail, Mike Rogers said the administration agreed to tariff Canadian trash trucks entering Michigan landfills; this may relate to the added 'waste products' but is unconfirmed.

items.text: On Oct 23 CMS proposed a rule requiring ACA Exchanges to verify eligibility before enrollment, implementing the Working Families Tax Cut Act. According to a law-firm summary, the rule would generally bar advance premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions while certain data matches remain unresolved. That could delay or deny subsidies for some marketplace enrollees during open enrollment. The same week HHS kept 2025 civil-penalty levels, and FDA finalized guidance on prescription-drug-use software.
items.outlet: Alston & Bird Health Care Week in Review
items.notes: I could not open the CMS press release or the Federal Register public-inspection PDF (2026-21891) because access was blocked, so the comment deadline and publication date are unverified.

items.text: Under its Closer to Zero initiative, FDA issued draft guidance setting action levels for cadmium in processed foods for babies and young children. It also issued a draft chapter on controlling chemical hazards in human food. FDA plans a webinar on Nov 16. Recalls posted Oct 22 include WinCo Foods hoagie rolls (undeclared sesame) and Natural Grocers 2-lb mung beans (possible glass).
items.outlet: AFDO summary of FDA constituent updates
items.notes: This comes from AFDO's digest of FDA's own updates; I did not open the FDA page directly. The comment period for the draft guidance is not stated.

items.text: The White House's presidential-actions page lists three Oct 22 actions. One is a proclamation 'Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines' under Section 232, which follows the Commerce investigation opened in 2025. The second is a Defense Production Act Section 303 determination on domestic petroleum production, refining and logistics. The third is an order titled 'Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People'. Together they point to more tariffs on wind equipment and federal support for oil capacity while the Iran war keeps fuel prices high.
items.notes: These were signed Oct 22, before the window, and could appear in the Federal Register Oct 23-27. I saw only the titles; tariff rates and other details are unverified because I could not open the texts or the Federal Register.

items.text: At an Oct 24 rally in Georgia, Trump announced a $4.2 billion Audi factory near Macon expected to create about 4,500 direct jobs. He also repeated his pledge of a $5,000 'Trump dividend' to adult citizens if Republicans hold both chambers, which he estimated would cost about $1 trillion, and warned of a '1929-style' depression under Democratic control.
items.notes: I found no Audi or Georgia state confirmation in the window. The dividend pledge dates from the September RNC convention and is not new. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's FOMC decision is due Oct 28 (see watch).

items.text: Alaska Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola and family members were hospitalized with minor injuries after a two-vehicle crash in Anchorage on Oct 24. Her campaign postponed some appearances.

The Polska 2050 board expelled Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, who resigned as minister of funds and regional policy and as party leader on Thursday 22 October. Szymon Hołownia announced the expulsion on Saturday. The party said she had acted against its interests and against resolutions of its statutory bodies. On social media she said she was being punished for a 'thoughtcrime' and suggested Hołownia's 'boss' would not appreciate his efforts. Deputy minister Jan Szyszko (Polska 2050) has also asked Tusk to dismiss him.
items.notes: Also covered by RMF24, TVN24 and wPolityce. TVN24 and wPolityce pages could not be opened, so the comparison relies on their headlines only. TVN24's headlines centre on coalition politicians' reactions, including Joanna Mucha blaming Pełczyńska-Nałęcz for destroying Polska 2050 and Arłukowicz asking why she was expelled. wPolityce frames it as a 'war in Polska 2050' with Hołownia 'raging' and mocks his explanation. Both agree on the basic facts.

items.text: In a Sunday post, Hołownia called the expulsion a 'natural consequence' of her actions. He said that only the party's National Council can decide to leave the coalition, and he criticised her for announcing her resignation on social media first. Senate deputy marshal Maciej Żywno told Polsat News that she plans to found a new association. Rzeczpospolita said the coming week is pivotal: Hołownia is demanding that the funds ministry stay with Polska 2050, and otherwise threatens to pull the party's ministers out of government while still backing it in the Sejm.
items.notes: The Rzeczpospolita piece by Michał Kolanko is paywalled; only its lead was read. Interia reports that Tusk has two female candidates for the ministry and will name one after returning from India. He has not said whether either comes from Polska 2050. The association claim rests on a single source (Żywno via RMF24/Polsat).

items.text: According to Rzeczpospolita (via money.pl), the government will try to use the Senate to undo two amendments the Sejm adopted against its wishes on 22 October. One scraps the planned rise in CIT from 19% to 22% for the largest firms. The other indexes PIT thresholds to inflation every year from 2028. Senate budget committee chair Kazimierz Kleina (KO) told Interia that the committee takes up the bill on Monday 26 October and that he expects the government's version to be restored. The Finance Ministry estimates the cost at 6.2 bn zł in 2027 and 3.8 bn zł in 2028.
items.notes: The amendments came from Ryszard Petru (Centrum) and Janusz Kowalski. XYZ puts the loss at about 32 bn zł over 2027–2030 from dropping the CIT rise alone. Any Senate amendment returns to the Sejm, which can reject it by absolute majority.

items.text: Polsat News reports that the government is weighing a 3% tax on the revenue of large global tech firms operating in Poland. The draft comes from the Ministry of Digital Affairs and would take effect on 1 January 2027. Deputy Sejm Marshal Marcin Horała said the idea is right in principle but would provoke a sharp US reaction, costing Poland more than it gains. He argued that an EU-wide levy would be better.
items.notes: The new element in the window is Horała's commentary. The draft's earlier publication date was not verified.

items.text: The two abortion bills the Sejm passed on 20 October now go to the Senate and then to President Nawrocki. The first restores abortion for severe foetal defects (233–203). The second partially decriminalises helping with an abortion (217–213). On Sunday, KO MP Dorota Łoboda told Polsat News she expects a veto, noting that Nawrocki pledged during his campaign not to sign any liberalisation. On 24 October, Polish bishops issued a statement on the new law that stressed doctors' duty of conscience.
items.notes: The bishops' statement was seen only as a Polsat headline and was not read in full. Right-leaning outlets (e.g. nczas.info) call the bill unconstitutional. Notes from Poland reported renewed street protests demanding further liberalisation on 23 October.

items.text: Częstochowa residents voted on Sunday to recall Mayor Krzysztof Matyjaszczyk (Lewica, suspended from the party) and the city council. About 97% backed the mayor's recall and 96.2% backed dissolving the council, on about 51,860 votes. The council vote cleared its 48,754 validity threshold. Matyjaszczyk was detained by the CBA in February and charged with corruption, which he denies. A commissioner appointed by the prime minister will run the city until early elections.
items.notes: Results come from the PKW/KBW. This follows Kraków's own recall of its mayor in May 2026.

items.text: Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka said the first SMR of European design should be built in Poland, at Włocławek, with more sites to follow. He cautioned that SMRs are not yet commercially proven. Earlier in the week, Orlen and Synthos Green Energy signed an umbrella agreement settling their ownership dispute. Under it, a company called BWRX-300 Włocławek (reportedly 70% Orlen, 30% SGE) will take the project forward toward a construction permit application to the PAA.
items.notes: The BWRX-300 is a GE Hitachi design. Polsat reports the 'European design' wording without explaining it. The shareholding split comes from Rzeczpospolita's sources and is not confirmed.

items.text: Germany has confirmed that the Bundeswehr will join the first joint exercise of the 'coalition of the willing' in November. Reported as 'Koalicja 2026', it will take place in Poland, in Romanian airspace and over the western Black Sea, and will rehearse moving troops and supplies for a possible future ceasefire-monitoring mission in Ukraine. Germany is sending about 10 staff officers and up to two A400M aircraft. The Times puts total participation at 1,500 or more troops from the UK, France and Germany, a figure not officially confirmed.
items.outlet: Polsat News (citing DW, The Times, dpa)
items.notes: No Polish troop numbers or exact dates were given.

items.text: IMGW issued level-II wind warnings for southern Silesia and Lower Silesia, with gusts up to 90 km/h and locally 100 km/h. Level-I warnings with gusts up to 80 km/h covered Małopolska (including the Kraków region), southern Podkarpacie and the coast, along with a Baltic storm alert. RCB sent an SMS alert to Bielsko-Biała and the Bielsko, Cieszyn and Żywiec counties. Polsat says the weekend marks a sharp turn to colder, wetter weather.
items.notes: No damage reports were found. nczas.info is a right-wing outlet, but here it is only relaying IMGW data.

items.text: GIS issued a statement on the first documented human infection with Shamonda virus, a livestock virus related to Schmallenberg. The patient, from Lyon in France, was immunocompromised and has died. GIS says the case looks isolated, that no human-to-human transmission has been documented, and that the risk to the Polish public is low. It is coordinating with the Chief Veterinary Officer, the WHO and the ECDC.
items.notes: The GIS statement itself was not opened, only Polsat's account of it. Regional outlets also report ongoing GIS recalls (Listeria in salami), but those date from before the window.

items.text: At a Nowa Lewica event in Lublin, Sejm Marshal Włodzimierz Czarzasty said that if President Nawrocki's closeness to Trump is real he should use it to help secure a permanent US base in Poland, and otherwise stop 'fawning' over Trump. Czarzasty also urged the coalition to return to its promises on women's rights and social security instead of courting the right and the Church, and warned of a growing Russian threat from drones near the border.
items.notes: These are political remarks, not a policy change.

items.text: Poland moved clocks back one hour to winter time overnight on 24–25 October under the EU summer-time directive. Polsat reported a matching autumn rail timetable correction, with some night trains halted for an hour. Talks on ending the twice-yearly clock change, including a Polish proposal to trial permanent summer time, have not produced an EU decision.
items.notes: The money.pl link is a background piece from October 2025. The Polsat rail article was seen only as a headline.

items.text: The Polsat News Ujawnia investigation 'Sztuka milczenia', aired Sunday, analysed salary data for about 3,000 hospital doctors obtained through hundreds of requests. It reports that some doctors earn millions of złoty, and that hospital directors admit to a 'pathological' pay system and have tried to keep the figures from coming out.
items.notes: This is Polsat's own investigation, and its figures are not independently verified.

items.text: Lawyers for Piotr W. filed a court complaint about how he was detained on 16 October during a protest outside the Constitutional Tribunal. Police say he pushed a female officer and was carrying a folding knife. A court had already refused the prosecutor's request to hold him for a month and released him without preventive measures, and the Human Rights Commissioner (RPO) has opened a case.
items.notes: Radio Maryja reports that opposition politicians are questioning the police intervention. The defence disputes the police account.

items.text: Mayor Łukasz Gibała's order abolishing all six remaining departments of Kraków City Hall (Civic Affairs, Kraków Brand, Sustainable Development, Municipal Services, Social Policy and Education) is due to be published on Monday 26 October. He signed it on Friday evening, 23 October, and announced it on social media. The six department directors lose their posts. The departments were set up by his predecessor Aleksander Miszalski and began operating in February 2025. Gibała had promised to abolish them during his campaign.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Reports do not say what happens to department staff or to the bodies the departments supervised, such as ZTP, ZDMK and schools. Readers' comments under the Radio Kraków piece are split between calling it a fix for overlapping responsibilities and calling it politically motivated. The order text itself was not seen in BIP.

items.text: Kraków's public transport authority (ZTP) has published the All Saints' Day transport plan. It runs from 24 October to 2 November and includes 8 special tram lines (81, 83–89) and 26 special bus lines in the 8xx series, serving 25 cemeteries. Extra service began on the weekend of 24–25 October, when tram 84 started running to Rakowicki Cemetery and every line 184 trip went to Prądnik Czerwony Cemetery. The full special timetable applies on 31 October and 1 November, when some regular lines are suspended or shortened. From 10:00 on 30 October, ul. Rakowicka is closed between Olszańska and Grochowska.

A revised Koleje Małopolskie timetable applies from 25 October to 12 December because of PKP PLK modernisation work, mainly on line 8 between Kraków and Kozłów (towards Miechów and Sędziszów). Stops will be longer and departure times may change roughly weekly. On the SKA1 Kraków Lotnisko–Kraków Główny line, service stops on the nights of 27–28 and 28–29 October: five trains are cancelled and replacement buses run.
items.notes: This comes from a small regional portal only. Passengers should check the Koleje Małopolskie website before travelling.

items.text: Reconstruction of ul. Nowohucka near ul. Koszykarska in Podgórze begins on Monday 26 October. The work adds a 50 m left-turn lane for eastbound traffic towards Stoczniowców and Saska, along with new signals, crossings, lighting and a bike path. In the first stage, pedestrians use a temporary walkway and the Nowohucka bus stop moves. A housing developer is paying for the project under an agreement with the city.
items.notes: No completion date has been given. The city says it will announce further traffic changes in stages.

items.text: Galeria Krakowska, the large shopping centre next to Kraków Główny station, reopens fully with normal hours on Monday 26 October. It had been closed since a fire in its car park on Wednesday 21 October, when people were evacuated.
items.notes: Known only from Gazeta Krakowska's press digest; the full article was not opened. The cause of the fire was not reported.

items.text: On Sunday 25 October, IMGW issued level-1 strong-wind warnings for southern Małopolska and southern Podkarpackie, with gusts of up to 80 km/h, valid until 21:00 at the latest. Neighbouring southern Śląskie and Dolnośląskie had level-2 warnings, and RCB sent phone alerts to the Bielsko-Biała area. No damage in Kraków was reported in the sources reviewed.
items.notes: The meteo.imgw.pl warning map was not checked directly, so it is unknown whether any warnings are still in force on Monday.

items.text: Several fatal and serious road accidents happened in Małopolska over the weekend. Around 02:00 on 25 October, a coach and a car collided on DW 772 in Prandocin, near Kraków: one person died and one was injured. On the evening of 25 October, a driver died in Stara Wieś (Limanowa county) after the car hit a tree. Separately, a car split in two in Brzoskwinia, about 15 km from Kraków, and its driver survived.
items.notes: The details come from press-digest summaries. Police statements were not checked.

items.text: Gazeta Krakowska reports that the city has changed the traffic layout at the al. Bora-Komorowskiego / ul. Stella-Sawickiego junction, which has many collisions and frequent traffic violations. Bus lanes are planned as the next step.

The 29th Kraków Book Fair (Targi Książki) closed on Sunday 25 October at EXPO Kraków. It had more than 1,000 authors and 500 exhibitors, and Olga Tokarczuk was among the authors drawing long queues. The same weekend, the 'Anna Jagiellonka' exhibition at Wawel (23 October 2026 to 14 February 2027) and a new Teatr Bagatela basement stage opened.

On 24 October, Wisła Kraków beat Raków Częstochowa 2:1 with a Kacper Duda goal in the 10th minute of stoppage time, in front of a sell-out crowd of about 33,000 at ul. Reymonta. Gazeta Krakowska reports that some fans chanted against Legia and insulted Left MP Anna Maria Żukowska. Separately, Cracovia lost 3:1 at Piast Gliwice, and its fans publicly attacked sporting director Filip Trubalski.

Gazeta Krakowska reports that the new water sports centre at Zakrzówek reservoir has opened under a private operator, and divers are already bringing in equipment. Residents meanwhile complain about cyclists riding through the area's forest paths and want better pedestrian safety.
items.notes: Signs at the entrance suggest only clients may enter. Who can access the centre is not yet clear.

items.text: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, speaking at a Patna event for the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first CM Shri Krishna Singh, replied to an audience member who said PM Modi would not go anywhere with a remark that 'even Modi's father' would go, according to PTI. He made it while vowing to jail those behind alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls. Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary and other NDA leaders condemned it. The BJP called protests at state and district headquarters for October 26 and demanded an apology, and a complaint was filed at Patna's Kotwali police station.
items.outlet: PTI via ThePrint / The Tribune; Business Today
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Business Today reports Congress defended the remark as a response to repeated provocation and stressed the SIR critique. It also notes unconfirmed reports that the heckler was assaulted. PTI copy carries no Congress response. The Scroll/The Hindu vs Swarajya comparison could not be done: no Swarajya piece on this turned up, and Scroll/The Hindu searches failed (proxy error).

items.text: Congress and INDIA bloc leaders are building up to a November 1 'Delhi Chalo' mega-rally at Ramlila Maidan against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged SIR irregularities ('vote chori'), ANI reports. A symbolic 'public impeachment' of the CEC is planned for October 30. Congress MP Deepender Hooda claimed that EC-BJP collusion has been 'exposed', and KC Venugopal reviewed mobilisation in Chandigarh ahead of a Rahul Gandhi rally on November 4.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: The collusion allegation is the opposition's claim and the article gives no evidence. No EC response was found. The Venugopal link was seen only as a headline.

items.text: On October 24 India's Consulate General in Jeddah issued a fresh advisory for Indian nationals, mostly Umrah pilgrims, stranded in Saudi Arabia after flights were cancelled following Houthi drone and missile attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure. The consulate runs 24x7 control rooms in Jeddah and Makkah and says it is providing food and medicines and coordinating with Saudi ministries and airlines. IndiGo has extended cancellations to Jeddah, Medina and Dammam until October 27 and to Riyadh until October 31, and Akasa has suspended Riyadh and Jeddah until October 27. On October 25-26 AIMIM's Asaduddin Owaisi urged the Centre to deploy aircraft to bring home about 4,000 pilgrims.
items.notes: RT (Russian state media) reports an Indian national was killed and two injured in a strike on Dammam's King Fahd airport around October 21, and that the MEA said about 3,000 pilgrims had returned in the past week. RT quotes a pilgrim saying the embassy had not contacted them, which conflicts with the consulate's account of active outreach. The 4,000 figure is Owaisi's. The ANI Owaisi article could not be opened.

items.text: Hereditary Prince Alois, Liechtenstein's acting head of state, arrived in Mumbai late on October 25 for a state visit running to October 28, according to the MEA schedule reported by ANI. After a stop in Vadodara he goes to Delhi. On October 27 he has a Rashtrapati Bhavan reception, talks with PM Modi at Hyderabad House, calls by Jaishankar and Sitharaman, and a meeting with President Murmu. ANI places the visit in the context of the India-EFTA TEPA trade pact, which took effect in 2025.
items.notes: TEPA isn't listed as a formal agenda item.

items.text: Indian equities opened lower on Monday October 26. Sensex fell about 609 points to 72,514 and Nifty about 133 points to 22,466 in early trade, Business Today reports. It cites Brent crude near $114 a barrel after a six-month high, a tech-led Asian sell-off and Nifty breaking key moving averages, while India VIX rose about 7% to 18. BSE market capitalisation fell by about Rs 3.14 lakh crore from October 23.
items.notes: These are intraday early-session figures, not the close. Another Business Today headline gave crude at $117.

items.text: DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla told Moneycontrol that the government plans to list three state-owned firms in FY27: IIFCL and Coal India subsidiaries Mahanadi Coalfields and South Eastern Coalfields, as reported by Business Today. MCL has filed its draft red herring prospectus. Chawla also flagged a second public highway InvIT and said the IDBI Bank stake sale to Fairfax should close by end-FY27, subject to RBI clearance.
items.notes: The figures come from an official's interview; no DIPAM release was found.

items.text: USCIS has started approving some H-1B petitions filed without the $100,000 fee, because federal courts have blocked its enforcement, Business Today reports. Indian professionals are the largest group of H-1B holders. Approvals are uneven, and the US government has appealed a Northern District of California order to the Ninth Circuit.
items.notes: This is a US development that matters to Indian workers. The source is an immigration law firm (Meltzer Hellrung) cited by Business Today.

items.text: Protesting students at Delhi's Jamia Millia Islamia rejected an October 26 university order as ambiguous and vowed to keep up their agitation, ANI reports. The order promises students' union elections 15 days after a union constitution is approved, revokes suspensions issued during the protest and sets up an inquiry into security staff. It also requires students to apologise publicly for posts against the administration. They want a firm written timeline and the Proctor's resignation.
items.notes: The university had not responded to ANI's request for comment.

items.text: Karnataka Deputy CM and Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara said severe drought has caused crop losses of up to 80% in some areas, ANI reports. He criticised the Centre for not releasing NDRF relief and urged the state's Union ministers, including H.D. Kumaraswamy, to help. The state announced Rs 1,250 crore in relief about a month ago, but disbursement is still pending, and a proposed all-party delegation has not been given an appointment in Delhi.
items.notes: The 80% figure is the minister's and no districts are named. No Union government response was found.

items.text: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar said he has granted prosecution sanction against suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in the KPSC recruitment-exam irregularities case, ANI reports. This allows the CID and ED to prosecute him under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The CID alleges he leaked papers for the January 2026 exam for 400 veterinary officer posts. Shivakumar promised to give the KPSC a 'new form'.
items.notes: The allegations come from the CID investigation as reported. The article spells the officer's name inconsistently.

items.text: PM Modi's 139th Mann Ki Baat radio address on October 25 highlighted rising Khadi and village-industry sales, ANI reports, including more than Rs 28 crore in a single day on Gandhi Jayanti. He urged people to buy local artisans' products in the festive season.
items.notes: Sector turnover figures come from the KVIC chairman, not the PM. The official transcript (PIB) could not be reached.

items.text: Delhi ministers visited the site of a building collapse in Harsh Vihar, where two people were feared trapped and rescue operations were under way, according to an ANI headline. Separately, ANI reported a major fire that gutted several shops at Shiv Market opposite Jammu railway station early on October 26.
items.notes: Based on headlines only; neither article could be opened. Casualty figures are unverified.

items.text: The IAF held a 'Wings over Ganges' aerial display in Varanasi featuring the Surya Kiran aerobatic team, with Army signals support, according to ANI headlines from October 25-26.
items.notes: Based on headlines only.

items.text: India's Asian Para Games medallists returned to Delhi and spoke about their results, according to ANI videos from October 24-25.
items.notes: No medal tally was verified.

items.text: US Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose posted on X (Friday 23 Oct, widely reported 24 Oct) that too many European leaders call Russia an existential threat but want America to confront it for them with US money and weapons, and accuse Trump of betrayal for pursuing peace. He held Poland up as the exception with the hashtag #belikePoland. PAP-based reports note the post came two days after envoy Witkoff's ninth Moscow visit; no direct reaction from Polish officials was reported.
items.notes: Post itself dated 23 Oct (just before window); coverage 24 Oct. Rose named no leaders. Context: ongoing friction between FM Sikorski and Washington/Musk over Starlink limits in Ukraine and a US deal on Russian diesel.

items.text: Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz told WNP.pl that a permanent US Army base would cost about 15 billion zł and that four sites west of the Vistula are in play: Wrocław, Poznań, Bydgoszcz and Szczecin. He said documents on US deployment directions go to the Pentagon in November, with a White House decision expected in December, and that the base could house about 5,000 soldiers (roughly 25,000 people with families and support staff). He stressed no final decision on whether or where has been made.
items.notes: Interview given 21 Oct, published 23 Oct, re-reported through 25 Oct (rp.pl updated 25 Oct, Wprost, Interia). Earlier (Sept) the deputy minister spoke of two sites; list has grown to four. Who pays is not stated. Pre-window item included because coverage continued into the window.

items.text: Polish prosecutors (Military Affairs Department, Warsaw District Prosecutor's Office) have closed with a final decision their investigation into the deaths of two GROM special-forces operators during a night HALO jump in Eloy, Arizona on 19 September 2025. They found the two jumpers collided after an unplanned change of positions and that no third party's actions or omissions caused the deaths.
items.notes: Exact date of the decision not given; spokesman prok. Piotr Skiba confirmed it is final. Also reported by WP and Interia.

items.text: After FM Radosław Sikorski again mocked Elon Musk on X (23 Oct) over WSJ reports that Musk ordered Starlink speed limits on Ukrainian drones, Trump said on Saturday he had spoken to Musk, and Musk admitted for the first time he had imposed the limits, blaming Ukrainian military misuse. Zelensky said service is back to normal.
items.notes: Polish angle is Sikorski's commentary; core story is US–Ukraine. SpaceX and White House accounts differ on whether Musk acted alone.

items.text: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will travel to Atlanta for the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting hosted by Secretary of State Rubio on 30–31 October, with a Quad foreign ministers' meeting expected on the margins. Reports say a Quad leaders' summit, the first in two years, is likely around 16 November in Manila during ASEAN meetings, though the date is not confirmed.
items.notes: No MEA press release seen yet. Rubio said on 22 Oct (ANI) that ASEAN meetings are 15–17 Nov but the summit date was not fixed.

items.text: A Hindi-language analysis says that despite Trump calling a deal very close and Rubio claiming about 99% of talks are done, no India–US trade agreement has been formally announced. It says New Delhi is still weighing conditions on agriculture (dairy, poultry, wheat, rice), domestic industry and data localisation, and that Russian oil purchases remain a friction point even after the US waived new Russian-oil tariffs in October.
items.notes: Status piece, no new development in window. Byline conflict (metadata says Suresh Prajapati). Background: Trump executive order of 16 Oct waived SRIA tariffs on Russian-oil buyers with no fixed expiry (Discovery Alert); some Hindi outlets describe it as a 60-day delay, so reports conflict.

items.text: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said on X that other states should follow Florida in stopping H-1B hiring at public universities. Florida's university system has a pause on new H-1B hires until 5 January 2027. Indians are the largest group of H-1B holders, and separate data reported this week show Indian F-1 student arrivals fell 39% year on year in August.
items.notes: State-level, not federal. The 39% figure comes from a less-established outlet (Gulte) that does not name its data source. Earlier, on 9 Oct, India called JD Vance's immigrant comments deeply offensive (CNBC).

items.text: Major League Baseball held its first MLBx Mumbai 3-on-3 event, with Indian cricketers including Suryakumar Yadav playing alongside former MLB players. US Ambassador Sergio Gor welcomed it on X.
items.notes: Soft-power item; no trade or policy content.

items.text: Polish drone maker WB Group plans to invest about $100 million over five years in unmanned systems in India through WB Electronics India, reportedly scouting sites in the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor and planning to export from India later, according to aggregator reports after PM Tusk's 21–23 October visit. NDTV had reported strong demand for Polish drones, and Tusk referred indirectly to the Indian army's use of Polish drones in last year's clashes with Pakistan.
items.notes: Neither outlet cites a primary source or spokesperson; treat the $100m figure as unverified until WB Group or an established outlet confirms it.

items.text: After Tusk's visit (joint statement 22 Oct: double trade by 2030, a Defence Industry Dialogue, a classified-information agreement 'soon'), XYZ's Asia correspondent wrote that Indian media covered it enthusiastically but largely repeated the government line, and gave little attention to the Ukraine war; Modi did not name Russia as aggressor. In Poland, right-leaning outlets criticised the visit, citing a roughly $3bn Polish trade deficit with India in 2024 (Nasza Polska) and alleged double standards over India's ties with Russia (wPolityce).
items.notes: Joint statement: https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/india-poland-joint-statement/ . The wPolityce article could not be opened; its framing is taken from the headline only. Nasza Polska names a PESA–Jupiter Wagons deal as the most concrete outcome but gives no value.
